title: Trapping Rain Water — Empty Elevation Map
problem: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map, compute trapped water.
intuition: Water requires at least two opposing boundaries and an intermediate dip.
invariant: When length < 3, trapped water is mathematically 0.

scenes.title: Test Case: Empty Elevation Map
scenes.narration: Testing input [] (Empty array (length 0). Invariant: no water can be trapped.). Expected output: 0.

dialogue.text: Evaluating test case 'Empty Elevation Map' with input: [].
How will our two-pointer invariant handle this boundary condition?

scenes.title: Corner Case Handled: Length 0
scenes.narration: Because length is 0 < 3, no two opposing walls can trap water. Returns 0 immediately.

dialogue.text: Zero water trapped. Empty array: 0 elements.
Correct. A container requires at least two boundary walls and one interior cell.
